title: tool.json
description: The entire coupling surface between a tool and this monorepo. Every gate in scripts/ is driven by this file, so a tool never has to restructure itself to participate. NOTE: this schema is for editor autocomplete and hover docs only. It is NOT the gate — scripts/lib/toolinfo.mjs is, because the checks that matter are cross-file (does the manifest exist, does every listed test path resolve, does the surface match the category directory) and no JSON Schema can express them. If the two ever disagree, toolinfo.mjs is right.

id.description: The STABLE PUBLIC HANDLE: git tags (<id>-v<version>), release artifact names, and the CI matrix are all built from it. Directories can be renamed; this cannot.

name.description: Product name as users see it, e.g. "FullShot".

surface.description: The delivery surface. Must equal the lowercased category directory: a tool under Extension/ has surface "extension". A category IS a delivery surface, not a product theme (spec §1.1).

summary.description: One sentence. Becomes the README catalog table cell.

aiHandoff.description: How this tool gets context out of the browser and into an AI assistant.

manifest.description: Path to the manifest, relative to the tool directory. The SINGLE source of truth for the version — there is deliberately no "version" key in this file (spec §3.1).

core.description: Which shared-core channel this tool vendors, or omit entirely if it vendors none.

channel.description: Directory under core/, e.g. "v1". Directory-as-major-version: a breaking change becomes core/v2 next to core/v1 and old tools keep running unchanged.

pin.description: null tracks the head of the channel. A version string pins it, so a core bump never forces retesting every tool the same afternoon.

package.description: What goes into the zip. A POSITIVE allowlist: a stray .md dropped into pages/ cannot ride along.

include.description: Exact paths, or directory prefixes ending in "/". _locales/ is collected unconditionally regardless of what is written here — see scripts/lib/toolinfo.mjs packagedFiles().

targets.description: Store targets built from this one tree.

chromium.description: Chrome and Edge receive the SAME, byte-identical file. Chrome Web Store allows 20 extensions per publisher and enforces that per publisher.

overlay.description: RFC 7386 JSON Merge Patch applied over the base manifest (spec §3.4). An overlay, not a duplicate manifest: a duplicate must be version-bumped twice, and one day it will not be.

tests.description: Node sims, run with no npm install, ever. A listed path that does not exist is fatal: a test path that no longer resolves does not fail, it silently stops running.

permissions.description: Every manifest permission mapped to why it is needed. Chrome review asks for these; keeping them here means the answer is versioned rather than retyped into a form.

broadHostJustification.description: Required before any STATIC host_permissions entry is allowed. optional_host_permissions needs no such justification, because the user grants it at runtime and can revoke it.

networkAllowlist.description: The machine-readable form of the marketing claim. An EMPTY array means CI fails the build on any network API in any packaged file, so "zero network calls" stops being a promise in a README and becomes a build gate.

listings.description: Store URLs, once live. null until then — never a guessed URL. THIS IS THE STORE VOCABULARY: check-catalog.mjs derives its host table from these keys, and check-store-metadata.mjs derives the expected storeMetadata.stores key set from them too. Adding a store starts here.

storeMetadata.description: The STORE axis. `targets` above is the BUILD axis and has two entries; this has three, because the chromium build ships to Chrome and Edge as two separate listings with different limits, different assets and different permanent ids. Store ids are NOT declared here — they come from `listings` above, and check-store-metadata.mjs holds the two to each other so a fourth list of store names cannot drift.

sharedDir.description: Listing material every store accepts — the 1280x800 screenshot set, the privacy-policy URL. Relative to the tool directory.

stores.description: One row per STORE. A store with no row is a store nothing checks.

build.description: Per-tool opt-in bundler, never a repo-wide decision. The repo must still clone-and-load with zero npm install (spec §2.4).

target.description: Which entry of `targets` builds the artifact this store receives. Chrome and Edge both name "chromium" — that is what makes the shared build a DECLARATION rather than a coincidence, and it is why three store rows cannot become three builds.

dir.description: Per-store listing directory, relative to the tool directory.

served.description: A GATE, not membership. false = the row records researched facts for a store not submitted to yet, and a missing directory PRINTS. true = the listing is live and a missing directory FAILS. This is what keeps owner-gated work (accounts, screenshots) from turning CI permanently red.

manifestPatch.description: Optional RFC 7386 merge patch applied for this STORE rather than this target. Edge requires update_url removed and the name de-Chrome-d; Chrome takes the base build unchanged.
